reason: OpenFloat saturates biased exponents to >=1; subnormal inputs are treated as min-normals (finding #3/#5/#6 exemplars). Unsupported by design; flagged as bug #6 where it corrupts magnitude.
OpenFloat has no NaN detection; exponent saturation maps NaN to max-normal magnitude (findings #1/#8/#10/#11).
OpenFloat has no infinity handling; same exponent saturation as NaN (findings #2/#7/#9/#12).
BUG, not a deviation: 0+0 returns 2.35e-38 (finding #13, min-normal*2 from exponent saturation). Excluded here only to characterize the remaining input space; tracked as open bug.

OpenFloat rounds by truncation, not RNE; accept 1 ulp on well-conditioned adds. NOTE: does NOT bound cancellation cases -- see open bug: near-cancellation amplifies truncation error without bound (2^19-ulp exemplar found at ulp<=16 sweep).
BUG, not a deviation: x + (-x) yields a large normal (3.17e+29 at e=0xf9) instead of +0; residual scales with operand exponent. Excluded only to characterize the rest; tracked as open bug.

OpenFloat cannot produce subnormal outputs; results that gradually underflow in IEEE are clamped to zero or min-normal of the same sign (finding: -6.02e-36 + 6.02e-36 -> min-normal instead of 9.18e-41).
